en.intro: Krishna asks you to listen for the exact chain of events that follows when tamas grows.
en.notice: Krishna lists four things born from tamas: darkness, inertia, negligence, and delusion. They arrive in sequence as the quality of tamas increases and takes over.
en.next: Sanjaya now describes what happens when sattva predominates at the time of death.
en.meaning: O descendant of Kuru, when tamas grows strong, darkness, inertia, negligence, and delusion arise.

en.intro: Krishna asks you to listen for the exact chain of events that follows when tamas grows.
en.body: O descendant of Kuru, when tamas grows strong, darkness, inertia, negligence, and delusion arise. Krishna lists four things born from tamas: darkness, inertia, negligence, and delusion. They arrive in sequence as the quality of tamas increases and takes over. Sanjaya now describes what happens when sattva predominates at the time of death.

hi.body: हे कुरुनन्दन, जब तमोगुण बढ़ता है, तो अप्रकाश, अप्रवृत्ति, प्रमाद और मोह ये वृत्तियाँ पैदा होती हैं। कृष्ण कहते हैं कि जब तमोगुण बढ़ता है, तो अप्रकाश, अप्रवृत्ति, प्रमाद और मोह ये चार चीज़ें पैदा होती हैं। अब सात्विकता के बढ़ने पर मृत्यु के समय क्या परिणाम होता है, यह बताया गया है।

issues: meaning_changed: "कृष्ण आपको यह सुनने को कहते हैं कि जब तमोगुण बढ़ता है, तो उसके बाद क्या-क्या होता है।" (The Hindi intro ('...सुनने को कहते हैं कि...') frames the verse as a command by Krishna to listen, which is an unsupported interpretation. The source verse is a direct statement of what happens when tamas grows, not an instruction to listen to the sequence of events.)

meaning_changed: "कृष्ण ने चार चीज़ों की सूची दी है जो तमोगुण के बढ़ने पर पैदा होती हैं: प्रकाश की कमी, काम न करने की स्थिति, लापरवाही और मोह।" (The notice claims Krishna 'listed' (सूची दी) the four things. In the source, Krishna is directly addressing Arjuna ('O descendant of Kuru') and stating that these things are born (जायन्ते) when tamas grows. It is not a third-person summary of a list, but a direct address of a causal process.)

borrowed: "next: When sattva grows, a different outcome appears at the moment of death." (The intro says 'Krishna asks you to listen for the exact chain of events that follows when tamas grows.' However, the 'next' field of this verse (verse 13) incorrectly describes the outcome when sattva grows (which is the subject of the NEXT verse, 14). It borrows the content of verse 14 and presents it as the next verse for verse 13.)
